title: Why the US Army is about to blow up nearly 10,000 pounds of unstable explosives in Iowa
description: A sign identifying the facility sits inside a fence surrounding the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa, on November 19th. | Photo: Getty Images Th

content.summary: A sign identifying the facility sits inside a fence surrounding the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa, on November 19th. | Photo: Getty Images The US Army is moving ahead with plans to detonate the nation's stockpile of lead azide at an ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa, at approximately 9:00AM CST on Wednesday. The Verge reached out to experts on what to expect, and will keep this post updated. What material is the Army planning to detonate? There are 68 drums holding about 9,700 pounds of lead azide, an unstable chemical compound created to detonate munitions like grenades.
